messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Stan - build a custom prior
parts:
Hello,

reading the reference manual (example link missing - page 179) and online resources I could not find the answer to my question. (the only information source that maybe I could relate to my issue is https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/4dwmJj1YwbsJ; message of Ben 1/7/13)

I have a linear regression defined between 1 and 4 (y = bx + c). I transformed this "line" in a probability density function (integral from 1 to 4 = 1). Now I would like to create this prior in Stan. Is this possible? What is the code relative to my example that does this.

y ~ my_density(b, c, 1, 4)

Furthermore I will eventually would like to create a quadratic custom function with the form y = ax^2 + bx + c

y ~ my_quad_density(a, b, c, 1, 4)

Thanks in advance.
Stefano

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan - build a custom prior
parts:
Check out the manual chapter on user-defined functions and
on variable transforms (there are examples of user defined
densities there).

The basic idea is to define a function to do it

functions {

real my_density_log(real y, real b, real c, real lb, real ub) {
compute log density and return
}

}

and then you can access it using sampling statements. And you better make
sure that y > 0 everywhere on the interval you care about or the density
won't make sense.

- Bob
